I found it really enjoyable up until about the mid game. Or what seemed like it. 

The building system is overall janky and the actual building components not that interesting. The biggest draw of building an intricate or cool base would be the pals and optimizing the workflow but the pal AI is incredibly inconsistent and stupid.

No priority system that the player can control to take the pal AI out of the equation either, pathing is a nightmare so if you decorate your base the smallest object could make areas "inaccessible" to the pals, and they wont work. 

Pals spawn first in the world I think, you consistently come into your camps to them being stuck on top of objects.

The hunger/food system feels like it could go away altogether and the game would lose nothing, food is tedious at best because the world overflows with things to eat. It'd be more interesting if the food gave stat buffs instead of having a hunger system imo.

December 2024 Update: I bought a SteamDeck this year, and the game plays beautifully on it!  My computer, despite meeting the minimum requirements, still just cannot keep up.  I am changing my recommendation to I would recommend with the caveat that you are using SteamDeck or XBox as I can verify gameplay on both of those platforms.

April 2024 Update:  I still cannot recommend this game on the PC for the reasons given in my initial review, however I do believe that people with a stronger PC should have much better results than me.  I have since had the opportunity to play this game on the XBox, and absolutely loved it!  I hope there will be some more tweaks that make the game more compatible for minimum spec computers to be able to play this game without all the crashes and bugs. I was pleasantly surprised by pal world. I think that this game is rather enjoyable and cheap at 40$ CAD for what it provides. This also provides some much needed competition for Nintendo and Game freak in the creature collector genre and this is something I always love to see. (Hopefully it paves the way for some more innovative and fun "Pokemon like" games as time progresses.) I don't want to compare this game to Pokemon too much but honestly this feels like what the 3-D more open world versions of Pokemon should look like. Props to Pocketpair for what they have created.

That being said this is an early access game and it shows. It feels like there is great potential for this to be a historical landmark in the creature collector genre. However, there a few things I would like to see improved in the coming months. 

Most importantly I would love to be able to play better on steam deck without regular crashes and raising the temperature of my room by five degrees. But I imagine this will come with time.
There should be a re-tuning of movement options, land mounts don't feel like they provide a significant enough speed boost to warrant ever using them, overall movement in the game feels very slow and could do with potentially an increase or other technology options to provide.
Additionally I would love to see an easier way to transport lots of materials to make base building or transferring between bases easier. I never feel like I have enough wood or stone to do anything with but it takes up nearly half of my max weight to carry those small amounts. I understand there is some cheese with the grapple gun but it feels almost janky or unintended. Maybe a tuning of the weights of items or another technology to make this easier.
Bases are another issue I want to mention, I find bases to be extremely buggy and frustrating to work with. My pals are regularly ending up stuck on something, dying for no reason, walking into fire, starving themselves, etc. I think an upgrade to the AI of the pals would help fix this issue first of all but pals aren't my greatest gripe with base building. 
This would in fact be the building itself. I don't feel like I can make anything creative or better than a little shoe box as the range of the palbox is too small for me to keep materials in my storage without being weighed down, and the building is much too rigid and finicky to work with. The range of the pal box also becomes an issue for building the functional parts of my base as my pals cant do anything with objects outside of range. Another issue is pals getting in the way of building causing me to not be able to place an object without getting rid of my pals. 
I would love to see some quests or more NPC's and locations to visit that don't feel so empty. At the moment exploring is slow and mostly seems useless outside of finding a few new pals and some of the green upgrade items. The idea of eggs, fruits, and chests is nice as it adds some variety to what else you can find but at the moment it just doesn't feel like enough. I think what I always loved about Pokemon is wandering into a cave and the potential that behind that corner i might wander into a legendaries lair or find some quest item.
This Segways into my next point, dungeons are interesting but ultimately feel kind of boring. Some more puzzles and different mechanics besides run in and kill everything in a room would make them astronomically more engaging.

If i were to boil that down into a condensed list/TLDR
the issues are
steam deck optimisation
movement/weight
building
AI
exploration
and how repetitive the game can feel

I would also again like to emphasise that I had a great time with palworld and there is quite a bit of potential here. I want so badly for this game to succeed and blow other creature collectors out of the water. Really set a new standard to move towards. I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone who has some interest in creature collectors with my only concerns being the issues highlighted above (that will likely be handled with time) and the apparent controversy around character designs (that I hope Pocketpair will address)

Palworld feels like a game full of good ideas and gameplay elements inspired by other great games.


[list]It has base-building, crafting, & survival elements[/list]
[list]It has monster catching and training[/list]
[list]It has base-management & work automation[/list]
[list]The combat is real-time and with guns[/list]


Unfortunately, the main gameplay elements of Palworld are very disjointed and feels very "tacked-on".

[list]Base-building, crafting, and survival are very basic and finicky and other games do it much, much better (e.g. Valheim)[/list]
[list]Base management & automation are mediocre at best and there doesn't seem to be any dedicated UI for managing tasks and assignments[/list]
[list]The combat and gunplay feels very janky. Enemy AI is not very and combat seems more like an exercise in tedium rather than an engaging activity. Animations are very mediocre and disjointed, especially jumping.[/list]
[list]The Pals feel very soulless. Pals exist to be caught, fought with, and employed; they do not have any meaningful interactions with one another and they do not feel like they "belong" in the world. The world doesn't feel "alive" and feels just like a big sandbox of several repeating assets sprinkled with Pals just walking around doing not much else.[/list]


Arguably, the only really good aspect of the game is being able to catch and battle monsters in real-time and having them do wacky stuff like shooting guns and all. And I think this is why it is such a big hit with streamers and with many players. The game looks incredibly wacky, fun, and meme-worthy and if folks enjoy it for this, then I have no issues with that and I respect it for what it is. But this game just isn't for the likes of myself who value depth and complexity in my games.

Please note that I went into this game as someone who had played a lot of survival, base-building, and simulation games so if it may seem that my review is unfair as I am holding the game to higher standards based on my previous experiences, then that is perfectly understandable.
